# Token Panorama for DSH
A DeepSeek Harness bundle that shows where every session's tokens go: one panel with lifetime totals

, a
calendar heatmap, a trend chart, a per-model breakdown, a per-session usage table, and CSV/JSON

export. Three
tool groups come with it: context clear/compact buttons, a prompt optimization button,

and auto answers for
`ask_user_question` batches while you are away.
Everything is read from the platform's own session persistence service, so nothing is scraped from l

ogs and no
third-party dependency is required.
## Features
- **Lifetime totals**: cumulative tokens, plus the input / output / cache-read / cache-write split a

nd call count.
- **Cache hit rate**: cache reads as a share of all input-side tokens, with absolute

hit and miss counts.
- **Cost estimate**: priced against DeepSeek's peak / off-peak bands, each band

's amount shown separately.
- **Calendar heatmap**: GitHub-style week columns or one mini calendar p

er month; switch with the `Week` /
`Month` control.
- **Trend chart**: daily / weekly / monthly / ye

arly granularity, with a hover readout per point.
- **Model breakdown**: tokens and calls per model,

sorted by volume.
- **Workspace breakdown**: grouped by the working directory each session header r

ecords, so you can see which
project costs the most.
- **Session usage tree**: main sessions only by

default; opening one reveals the subagent sessions it owns, so
the card does not grow with the suba

gent count. Sortable by column, archived sessions marked and hideable,
and row figures follow the se

lected date range.
- **Paging**: 40 session groups per page, so a large history never renders every

row at once.
- **Shared time range**: the filter bar is the one control every card reads (All / Toda

y / Last 24 hours /
This week / Last 7 days / This month / Last 30 days, plus a pair of date inputs)

. The heatmap, trend, cost,
peak, model, session and workspace cards all recompute from the same spa

n.
- **Hourly axis**: narrowing to Today or Last 24 hours switches the trend card to hours, filling

in the quiet
hours so the line cannot cut across an idle stretch.
- **Export**: daily buckets as CSV

(UTF-8 BOM + CRLF) or JSON, plus a separate per-session CSV with the
workspace, parent session, and

cost columns.
- **Incremental refresh**: a per-session revision token decides what to re-read, so a

refresh only decodes
sessions that actually changed.
- **Holiday auto-update**: any year is fetched

at runtime and cached, so a new year needs no new build.
- **Context actions**: Clear (orange) and

Compact (green) buttons in the dock under the composer, plus the

## Requirements

- DSH `>= 0.2.1-rc.3` (declared as `dsh.engines.dsh`).
- A profile whose client runs the Web UI; the
bundle registers into `sidebar.panellist` and `main`.
## Install
Install from a local directory through the Plugins page or the plugin manager, pointing at the packa

ge
directory (the folder containing `package.json`):
[代码示例省略，未执行]
After installation the sidebar shows a **Token Panorama** entry; selecting it opens the main panel.
To remove it, uninstall the `dsh-token-panorama` bundle from the Plugins page.
## npm package

The plugin is also published to the public npm registry as `dsh-token-panorama`. Storefronts
(the aw

esome-dsh-plugin catalog and the in-app market) can then install it by package name
and show a downl
oad figure, instead of falling back to the GitHub Release tarball.

- Publish a new version with `npm publish --access public`. npm requires either two-factor
authentic

ation or a granular access token with Bypass 2FA enabled.
- The catalog reads the `name` field of th

e repository `package.json`, confirms that package on
the registry, and requires the npm package `re

pository` field to point back at this GitHub
repo. The mapping is discovered automatically; no field

needs to be added to any listing.
- The download figure is the npm download count over a rolling 30

-day UTC window
(`api.npmjs.org/downloads/point`), refreshed by the catalog nightly probe. It is not

a
page-view or visit count: neither the catalog nor the market exposes any view metric.
GitHub Rele

ase asset downloads are a separate number and do not feed this field.
- Every change bumps `version`

in `package.json`; publish that version too, so the registry
`latest` tag and the catalog `version`

son`; publish that version too, so the registry
`latest` tag and the catalog `version` stay in step.
## Usage

1. Select **Token Panorama** in the sidebar.
2. Choose a range from the filter bar, or type a `From`

/ `To` pair.
3. Switch the heatmap between `Week` and `Month`, and the trend between `Hour` / `Day`

/ `Week` /
`Month` / `Year` (`Hour` appears only on a sub-day range).
4. Hover any trend point for

its exact numbers.
5. The **Session usage** tree lists main sessions by default. Select the `▶` at t

he start of a row to open it,
revealing every subagent session it owns. Select a column header (Sess

ion / Tokens / Calls / Created) to
sort, clear `Show archived` to see only sessions still in use (th

e choice is remembered across visits), and
use `Export sessions CSV` to save what the table currentl

y shows.
6. Page through large histories with `Previous` / `Next`; each page holds 40 session groups

.
7. Use **Refresh** to re-scan, or **Export** to save the daily buckets as CSV / JSON.
8. Use **Gen

eral settings** to open the settings window and change the zone, currency, peak windows, holidays,
a
nd price sheet; saving re-prices immediately.
The panel refreshes automatically when it opens; large histories load in about a second because only

changed
sessions are decoded after the first pass.
## Billing configuration
Every billing parameter is a plugin config entry. Open the settings window from the `General setting

s` button
in the panel header to edit them online; saving re-prices immediately, with no DSH restart

` button
in the panel header to edit them online; saving re-prices immediately, with no DSH restart.
The window edits the config by structure, not by field name: model prices are a table, peak schedule

s are
reusable profiles, and holidays are a checklist, none of which a generic key/value editor can

express. It has
seven tabs:
